source: Hacker's Delight, 2nd ed. (H. S. Warren), section 5-2 "Parity"
description: Naive xor of the 8 bits of a byte not folded to ctpop & 1
notes: Found while screening C candidates: the better version is the standard one (also Bit Twiddling Hacks #ParityNaive, popcnt on skylake). Naive xor of all bits written by us. clang trunk -O3 -march=skylake does not form ctpop: the SLP vectorizer turns the shifts into an <8 x i32> lshr and llvm.vector.reduce.xor: 7 IR instructions. expected.ll is ctpop.i8 & 1, zero-extended: 4 IR instructions. Different fold from popcount-bits-u8 (xor of the bits instead of their sum). No LLVM issue found for this idiom. Gain estimated by llvm-mca (godbolt llc and llvm-mca trunk, -mcpu=skylake, cycles per 100 iterations): 538 vs 110. expected.ll proven correct (refinement) by Alive2 alive-tv, 2026-10-28: src = clang trunk -O3 IR of src.c (godbolt cclang_trunk, -O3 --target=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -march=skylake -emit-llvm -S -g0) renamed @src, tgt = expected.ll renamed @tgt, identical signature; output 'Transformation seems to be correct!' with no warning. Run on Alive2's own Compiler Explorer instance (alive2.llvm.org/ce, compiler id 'alive'), since godbolt.org does not host alive-tv.
